name: promtool binding bypassed
explanation: The ledger test a promtool witness whose text appears only outside a real case comment is unresolved (scripts/g17-first-failure-ledger.test.mjs) fails with an AssertionError when the alertCaseBound gate is bypassed. The earlier SURVIVED rows (contract-reconcile-2) were produced before this test existed: it was added in cc80be0 (2026-11-17 00:26 local commit time), after that round.
demonstration: retest/frozen: 64 of 64 control, mutant exit 1 with 1 failing test, 64 of 64 control after.

name: manifest rejection binding bypassed
explanation: The ledger test the manifest-rejection witness is unresolved when any of its three Node cases did not execute fails when the manifestRejectionBound gate is bypassed. Same explanation as M01: the test post-dates the earlier round.
demonstration: retest/frozen: 64 of 64 control, mutant exit 1 with 1 failing test.

name: extracted files not compared by size
explanation: The next branch of the same else-if chain compares the SHA-256 of the extracted file. Two byte strings of different length cannot have the same SHA-256 (collision resistance), so a size difference is always reported by the hash branch. The verdict (ok false) is identical for every input; only the wording of the problem changes. The earlier layer (entry size from the zip table against the inventory) also reports it.
demonstration: proofs/archive-demo.json: five honest tamper cases and three simulated extractor failures (extra file, skipped file, truncated file); the M03 verdict equals the original verdict in all eight.

name: extra extracted files tolerated
explanation: Every file the standard reader (System.IO.Compression ExtractToDirectory) writes corresponds to an entry of the zip table, and the entry loop already reports any entry that is not in the inventory. The guard can only fire if the extractor writes a file that has no entry. Residual: under a simulated misbehaving extractor that plants an extra file the mutant accepts the archive (verdict differs); no input that the standard reader produces reaches this difference. No executable change was made. This is a disclosed non-material residual for S25-A02.
demonstration: proofs/archive-demo.json: honest reader cases identical; simulated extra file: original false, M04 true.

name: unextracted files tolerated
explanation: With the guard disabled the else-if chain dereferences found.bytes on an undefined value, which throws a TypeError that the surrounding catch converts into a problem. The verdict is therefore still ok false for a file that was not extracted. The entry-table check inventory file missing from the archive reports the same condition earlier.
demonstration: proofs/archive-demo.json: simulated skipped file: original false, M05 false.

name: project label not compared (container)
explanation: Containers are listed with docker ps --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=<Project>. The daemon matches the label value exactly, so every returned container carries exactly Project and the in-script comparison cannot be false. The real daemon (Docker 29.9.2) was shown to return only the exact value and not the case, whitespace, prefix, suffix or substring variants.
demonstration: proofs/label-filter-demo.out.txt and proofs/own-label-demo.json: near-miss decoys never reach the guard; original and mutant return identical inventories.

name: network label project not compared
explanation: Same as M06 for docker network ls --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=<Project>.

name: residual resources tolerated
explanation: Real defect class: containers that docker reports as removed but that remain (or that appear again) were reported as success. Nothing in the frozen tests exercised the post-removal re-enumeration. New behavioural control: containers that docker reports as removed but that remain make the cleanup fail instead of reporting success.
demonstration: candidate: control 12 of 12, mutant exit 1 on the new test, control after 12 of 12.

name: address range release not proven
explanation: Real defect class: the address range being taken by another network right after removal went unreported. The frozen tests only exercised Test-G17SubnetFree separately. New behavioural control: an address range taken by another network right after the removal fails the cleanup and names the holder.
demonstration: candidate: control 12 of 12, mutant exit 1 on the new test, control after 12 of 12.

name: volumes removed with containers
explanation: On the frozen source the mutant is detected only by a source-text assertion (the runner preserves before it removes test greps for rm -v). That is not a behavioural detection: only named volumes were ever created and docker rm -v does not remove named volumes. New behavioural control: a container with a docker-created anonymous volume is cleaned up and the volume must still exist.
demonstration: candidate: control 12 of 12, mutant exit 1 with both the textual test and the new anonymous volume test failing.

name: existing evidence directory overwritten
explanation: Locator defect in the earlier round: the guard is in scripts/cleanup-g17-owned.ps1 while the mutation config targeted g17-docker-ownership.ps1, so the pattern was never applied. Applied to the right file the mutant survived on the frozen source because the test only matched already exists, which the generic New-Item error also contains. Behaviour is verdict-equivalent (New-Item refuses an existing directory, nothing is written, exit 1), but the refusal is the script's own documented message. The test now asserts the Never overwrite evidence text and that no record is written.
demonstration: proofs/m11-m17-demo.json: original and mutant both exit 1 with the evidence directory byte-identical; the error source differs (explicit throw versus New-Item). candidate: mutant exit 1 on the tightened test.

name: exit of children not awaited
explanation: The producer reads process identity through Get-CimInstance Win32_Process, which does not exist on this Linux host. The control (1 test) fails before any mutation (exit 1) so the mutant was not counted. The existing test cannot tell the mutant apart on Windows because Stop-Process -Force terminates a stand-in promptly; a negative control needs a child that outlives the stop request for a few seconds (design in section 7 of the retest record). Not retestable here.
demonstration: retest/frozen: control exit 1, Get-CimInstance not recognised.

name: lingering child tolerated
explanation: Same platform block as M12. The guard is reached only when the wait ends without the timeout error while the child is still present, for example when Wait-Process fails with an error other than the timeout (swallowed by the empty catch). No current test provides that condition (design in section 7 of the retest record). Not retestable here.
demonstration: retest/frozen: control exit 1, Get-CimInstance not recognised.

name: stream names accepted
explanation: The mutation removes the colon from the first-character class of the hash list line pattern. The existing test used a colon only in the middle or at the end of a name, so a name that starts with a colon was accepted undetected on the frozen source. New cases : leading, : and :: were added to the colon position test.
demonstration: candidate: control 17 of 17, mutant exit 1 on the colon position test.

name: stream names accepted (second position)
explanation: Supplementary retest of the same mutation applied to the last-character class (the pattern has two occurrences). The existing ends: case detects it. Recorded so that both occurrences of the locator are accounted for.
demonstration: frozen: exit 1 on the colon position test; candidate: same.

name: bom not stripped
explanation: The earlier PATTERN_NOT_FOUND rows came from a source revision before the BOM strip existed (introduced in ca14bcf, 2026-11-16 23:54; the verifier rounds ran earlier). On the frozen source the original locator occurs exactly once and the mutant is killed by 16 failing assertions, including the explicit a byte order mark on the state file is tolerated test.

name: marker may be non-comment text
explanation: Not equivalent. Without the comment requirement a marker in non-comment text becomes the anchor: (a) an earlier mention of the marker hides the real comment that follows (alertCaseBound true becomes false), and (b) a marker trailing the interval line itself anchors a block that has no comment above it (false becomes true). Neither was tested. New tests cover both.
demonstration: candidate: control 11 of 11, mutant exit 1 with 2 failing tests.

name: block start not required
explanation: At the production boundary alertCaseBound the guard is redundant: with no block start the slice is empty or a single line, which can never contain input_series followed by a series line, so alertCaseBound is false either way (0 differences in 80004 generated comparisons). At the exported alertCaseBlock the result differs (null versus an empty or single line string). A test now asserts null for a case comment with no block after it.
demonstration: proofs/m11-m17-demo.json; candidate: control 11 of 11, mutant exit 1 on the new test.
